report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a specific, reproducible difference: Model B (minus A) pushes logits toward vocabulary about professional/technical/academic status and culinary/cooking/restaurant concepts, especially on the early output tokens. I cannot, from this evidence alone, say why (i.e., what training objective changed), only that the residual-stream difference consistently points toward those token clusters.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial pattern: the L2-norm of the difference is very small in early layers and then grows, peaking in late layers (notably layers 24–25, and large at layers 20–23 as well). The strongest concentration is at early token positions (pos1 and pos0/pos2 in several late layers) — i.e., the change is injected into the part of the residual stream that affects the first few tokens of a continuation.
- Logit-lens tokens: across the highest-norm (layer,position) cells, the top tokens the difference points to are repeatedly in two clusters:
  - professional/technical/academic: "professional", "Professional", "professionalism", "professionalism", "technical", "Technical", "dissertation", "doctoral", "undergraduate", "professionalism", "quantitative", "Research/Res", "Engineering".
  - culinary/cooking/restaurant: "Cook", "Cooking", "cooking", "culinary", "restaurant", "baking", "Cake", "microwave", "hot", "kitchen", "Chef".
  Many cells at late layers and early positions list tokens from one or both of these clusters, suggesting the difference reliably increases logit mass on these concepts.
- Patchscope: no continuation readouts were provided, so behavioural confirmation via generated text is missing; the logit-lens + norm pattern is the basis for the claim.

Caveats / limits
- I do not have direct generated continuations (patchscope outputs) to show that completions are actually steered to those topics in context; the logit-lens evidence is strong but not an execution-level proof of changed end-user behaviour.
- The evidence does not point to a single training objective or intentional feature (e.g., "made more professional-sounding"); it only shows a change in activation space that would bias early-token outputs toward the noted vocabulary clusters.

Short summary
- Model B upweights vocabulary related to professional/academic status and to culinary/cooking/restaurant topics (vs A), primarily affecting the first few tokens of continuations (signal concentrated in late layers, early positions).
